messages:
maria: Hey team — Customer FinAnalytics is hitting a streaming cutoff during long generations (~25-40s). They set a client timeout but streams are disconnecting after ~10s with a ReadTimeout / stream closed error. Repro + logs below, filing escalation now.

maria: Repro (python):
```py
import os
from redwood import RedwoodClient
os.environ['REDWOOD_TIMEOUT'] = '10'  # customer said they set this
client = RedwoodClient(api_key='sk-...', timeout=30)
for chunk in client.stream(model='gpt-large', prompt='long reply please'):
    print(chunk.text)
```

maria: Stack snippet: `ReadTimeoutError: Stream read timed out after 10s` then `ConnectionClosedError: remote closed stream` — even though model keeps generating on server side. Customer SDK version: 0.9.3. They think `timeout=30` should cover long gens.

alex: Do we know whether they're using `client.stream` (server-sent events) or our chunked websocket? Also need full SDK version + full trace.

maria: They confirmed `client.stream` (HTTP SSE). Trace attached: shows internal chunk loop raising at client/_stream.py:187 `await resp.content.read()` -> timeout. They also set REDWOOD_TIMEOUT env var (see repro).

sam: FYI — current behavior (pre-0.9.5) has multiple timeout knobs and precedence is confusing: env var REDWOOD_TIMEOUT overrides client-level `timeout` for connection/read timeouts. Separately, streaming uses a per-chunk timeout (default 10s) to avoid hanging connections if a model stalls between chunks. If a model doesn't emit a chunk for >10s, we close. That's why they're seeing 10s cutoffs even though client.timeout=30.

sam: Quick workaround: pass an explicit stream chunk timeout when constructing the client:
```py
client = RedwoodClient(api_key='sk-...', timeout=(5, 60), stream_chunk_timeout=60)
# timeout tuple = (connect, read) for underlying HTTP lib; stream_chunk_timeout is applied per chunk
```

sam: Or unset the env var in their process (delete REDWOOD_TIMEOUT) so the client-level value wins. We'll ship a fix to make precedence less surprising and surface the stream chunk timeout in docs. Patch targeted for 0.9.5.

maria: Thanks — customer tried `stream_chunk_timeout=60` locally and that prevented the cutoff. They want to know why `timeout=30` alone didn't apply. Can we fix to treat `timeout` as a global cap?

alex: Short explanation to customer: `timeout` in the Python SDK historically maps to the underlying request connect/read tuple (or requests-style single number), while streaming has a separate safety cutoff. We keep chunk timeouts to avoid leaked connections from hung models. Changing semantics could regress other customers who rely on short chunk timeouts. We'll propose an ergonomics change (global `global_timeout_for_generations`) but need an internal review.

dev-bot: [ticket-4519] reproduction recorded: https://internal/infra/repros/4519 (attached reproduction script + model logs) :white_check_mark:

alex: For immediate production mitigation advise them to either: 1) set `stream_chunk_timeout` to a higher value, or 2) use non-streaming `client.generate()` and poll for output (this will keep the single request alive under the top-level timeout), or 3) remove REDWOOD_TIMEOUT env var.

support_lead: Please open an internal issue documenting: a) surprising env var precedence, b) stream chunk timeout not obvious in docs, c) suggested API ergonomics. Include repro, tests, and test plan. Mark P2 for customer SLA.

maria: Will open issue + update customer with the workaround (stream_chunk_timeout) and ETA 0.9.5 patch. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sam: Adding note — also add a debug log around "last chunk received at T" so support can see inter-chunk gap durations in future tickets.

maria: Added to the ticket notes. Closing here for now, will post updates when patch merges.
